review: Stanzas 1–5 all open on بِحُبِّكَ السَّامِي ('in Your sublime love'); the Hebrew repeats בְּאַהֲבָתְךָ הַנִּשְׂגָּבָה at the same points, and stanza 6 carries it into the third line because the Arabic moves it there for the closing thanksgiving.
1:3 הִתְרוֹקַנְתָּ — 'You emptied Yourself' (Phil 2:7, הִפְשִׁיט אֶת־עַצְמוֹ); the Arabic أَخْلَيْتَ نَفْسَكَ is the kenosis verse, and the hithpa'el of רוקן keeps the reflexive force.

2:3 עֶבֶד מַקְשִׁיב תָּמִים — 'a fully obedient slave', for عَبْدًا مُطِيعًا كَامِلًا; מַקְשִׁיב ('listening') carries עבד's sense of hearing and obeying better than a bare adjective, and תָּמִים carries 'complete'.
3:2 בִּמְקוֹם־אַשְׁמֵנוּ — 'in our guilty place'; the Arabic مَقَامَنَا الْأَثِيم is the substitution of hymn 43:4, and Hebrew keeps the construct with אַשְׁמֵנוּ for the same doctrine.
5:2 נִתְּנוּ לָנוּ כָל־הַבְּרָכוֹת — 'all blessings were given to us'; the Arabic وُهِبْنَا كُلَّ الْبَرَكَات is a passive with a dative, which Hebrew reproduces with the niphal plus לָנוּ.
